statement.p: Calculate the integral of f(x,y,z) = 5 x^2+5 y^2+z^{9} over the curve \mathbf{c}(t) = (\cos t, \sin t, t) for 0\le t\le \pi.

static.solution:
[Step 1.] Compute \|\mathbf{c}'(t)\|.
We differentiate \mathbf{c}(t): \mathbf{c}'(t)=\frac{d}{dt} \left\lt \cos t,\sin t,t \right> = \left\lt -\sin t,\cos t,1 \right> Hence, \|\mathbf{c}'(t)\| = \sqrt{(-\sin t)^2+\cos^2t+1^2} = \sqrt{\sin^2t+\cos^2t+1} = \sqrt{2} \,ds = \|\mathbf{c}'(t)\| \,dt=\sqrt{2} \,dt [Step 2.] Write out f\left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right).
We substitute x=\cos t, y=\sin t, z=t in f(x,y,z)= 5 x^2+5 y^2+z^{9} to obtain f\left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right)=5 \cos^2t+5 \sin^2t+t^{9}=5+ t^{9} [Step 3.] Compute the line integral.
Using the Theorem on Scalar Line Integrals we obtain \int_{\mathcal{C}} (5 x^2+5 y^2+z^{9}) \,ds = \int_0^{\pi} f\left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right)\|\mathbf{c}'(t)\| \,dt = \int_0^{\pi} (5+ t^{9})\sqrt{2} \,dt =\sqrt{2}\left(5 t+\frac{t^{10} }{10}\right)\bigg|_0^{\pi} = \sqrt{2}\left(5 \pi+\frac{\pi^{10} }{10}\right)
